h: Dinosaurs, Chines and the Island Steam Line
p: Wildheart has a different feel from a traditional zoo because every animal is a rescue, so take the time to read their stories as you go round. It makes the visit far more meaningful and gives children plenty to talk about afterwards. The sanctuary's compact size means you can take things slowly and still see everything, so there's no need to rush.

Big cats spend a fair bit of the day snoozing, so catching a talk or feeding time is your best bet for seeing them on the move. On a summer holiday, think about going early or later in the afternoon when the beach crowds are busy elsewhere, and bring a layer, because the breeze off Sandown Bay can be sharp even in sunshine.

Sandown has plenty to keep families busy beyond the sanctuary. Dinosaur Isle, a purpose-built museum shaped like a giant pterosaur, sits on the seafront and showcases the Isle of Wight's rich fossil heritage. The island is famous for its dinosaur fossils, and the museum runs fossil-hunting walks along the coast.

Further along the coast, Shanklin Chine is a dramatic wooded ravine with waterfalls and paths, lit up beautifully on summer evenings. For a nostalgic day out, the Isle of Wight Steam Railway runs vintage trains between Smallbrook Junction and Wootton through peaceful countryside. Culver Down, at the northern end of Sandown Bay, offers sweeping views across the island and the Solent, especially beautiful at sunset.

For a car-free day, Island Line trains run between Ryde Pier Head and Shanklin, calling at Sandown on the way, so you can step off the ferry at Ryde and be among the big cats without touching a steering wheel.
